prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Miami after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — quick question before I give a tailored list: was anyone seriously injured (hospitalized or catastrophic injury), or is this a minor injury/property-damage case? Also do you need Spanish‑speaking counsel or any other preference (trial lawyer vs. quick settlement)?

While you answer, here are a few reputable Miami/South Florida personal-injury firms you should consider calling and why — plus what to ask and bring to your first (usually free) consult.

Recommended firms to call (with why)
- Morgan & Morgan (Florida offices, including Miami area)
  - Very large national firm with substantial resources, lots of experience in car-accident cases, and trial capability if the insurer won’t settle. They handle high volumes and often have bilingual staff.
- Kanner & Pintaluga (South Florida–based)
  - Regional firm known for handling serious car-accident and catastrophic-injury cases and for taking cases to trial when needed. Good local courtroom experience.
- Steinger, Greene & Feiner (Florida personal-injury firm)
  - Focuses on auto accidents and personal injury across Florida; known for aggressive client representation and contingency-fee arrangements.
- Anidjar & Levine (Florida firm with Miami presence)
  - Handles car accidents, wrongful death, and catastrophic injuries across Florida; known for client outreach and contingency representation.

Also consider:
- Using the Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service or Miami-Dade Bar Association referral — both can connect you to board-certified personal-injury attorneys near you.
- Looking up attorneys on Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, or Google Reviews to check client feedback and disciplinary history.

What to ask during the initial call/consultation
- Have you handled car-accident cases like mine (similar injuries, liability issues)? How many?
- Will an attorney (not a paralegal) handle my case and who will be my main contact?
- Do you take cases on contingency (no upfront fee) and what is your contingency fee/expense arrangement?
- Do you have trial experience? Do you expect this to settle or go to trial?
- What kind of recovery might be realistic for my injuries (very general ballpark)?
- How long do you expect this case to take?

What to have ready for the call/consult
- Date/location/time of accident, police report number (if available)
- Photos of vehicle damage and injury, witness names/contacts
- Insurance information (your policy and the other driver’s)
- Medical records/ER records or list of treatments and providers
- Any correspondence from insurers

Red flags to watch for
- Firm guarantees a specific dollar amount or guarantees a win.
- Pushy upselling of “you must sue” without reviewing facts.
- Lack of willingness to put things in writing about fees and who handles the case.

If you want, tell me:
- the neighborhood in Miami, severity of injuries, and if you prefer Spanish-speaking counsel — I’ll produce a short, customized list with phone numbers and suggested first-call scripts for 3–5 lawyers.
